newsitem.title: USA: Technology group pushes Nasdaq to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Technology group pushes Nasdaq to higher close.

text.p: High techs led Nasdaq stocks to a higher close on Wednesday as an encouraging August book-to-bill ratio sparked interest in the group.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 4.53 points, or 0.39 percent, at 1153.96 at its unofficial close. Gainers led losers by 2032 to 1997 on volume of about 492 million shares.

The book-to-bill index rose to 0.90 in August from a revised 0.86 in July. Though still fairly weak, the index's improvement during a seasonally slow month was a positive development for the troubled semiconductor sector.
Electronics for Imaging Inc was up 5-3/4 at 72. Prudential Securities raised the stock to buy from hold, saying it expected the company to beat third-quarter estimates.
Dell Computer was up 2-1/2 at 73-1/2 after saying it cut prices again on its line of network-ready Dell OptiPlex desktop personal computers by up to 16 percent.
Itron Inc tumbled eight points to 21 after the company warned that its results would fall short of expectations for a second quarter in a row.
Quality Systems Inc was down 2-5/8 at 8-1/8 after Pacific Growth Equities cut its revenue and earnings growth estimates for fiscal 1997 and 1998.
